items.why: The report says I_D/I_G "rises from 0.250 to 0.570 to 1.19 across doses 1–3" and D' heights grow from 114 to 430. G FWHM is 13.8 cm⁻¹ and the 2D band stays single-layer-like ("2D FWHM = 32.1, 31.9, 31.9"), and the report calls doses 1–3 stage 1 with defect density rising.
It gives I_D/I_G = 0.250, 0.570 and 1.19 with "L_D ≈ 24, 16 and 11 nm" from Cançado 2011 at 532 nm, all within the rubric ranges.
It uses "L_D² = 1.8e-9·λ⁴/(I_D/I_G)" with "λ⁴ = 8.01e10 nm⁴ at 532 nm", which is the wavelength-dependent form rather than 514.5 nm constants.

It says "Dose 4 is past the D/G maximum", with G ~3.3× wider, D' degenerate with the broad G, and "2D is essentially gone". It calls this stage 2 with the crossover "near L_D ≈ 3 nm", says "the L_D formula does not apply there" and that dose 4 "has the most disorder".

It finds I_D/I_D' ≈ 6.2–6.9, "in the range associated with vacancy-like defects". But it gives Eckmann's other values the wrong way round ("≈13 for boundaries… ≈3.5 for sp³"), and it does not note that the ratio is only valid at low density.
It states "peak heights from Lorentzian fits" and reports that "Area-based ratio gives 0.27, 0.61, 1.26, 0.74", so it makes the heights-versus-areas difference explicit.

It asks "What is the 'dose' physically (ion, electron beam, plasma, laser exposure, chemical)?" but only so it can convert to defects per dose, not because the point-defect assumption or defect type depends on it.

wrong_claims.why: It says dose 4 "has the most disorder" and does not compute an L_D for it.
It computes L_D with λ⁴ at 532 nm. The Tuinstra–Koenig L_a values appear only as an alternative-calibration caveat, and they also use λ⁴.
The 2154 cm⁻¹ spike is not mentioned or assigned anywhere.
